title: NY State Senate · District 10
area: Southeast Queens, including the Rockaways, Far Rockaway, Rosedale, Springfield Gardens, Jamaica and Laurelton.

context.text: James Sanders Jr. advanced from the Democratic and Working Families Party primaries without appearing on the ballot; no candidate filed to run against him in the June 23, 2026 primaries or in the general election.

summary.text: James Sanders Jr. is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for NY State Senate District 10, first elected in 2012. He chairs the Senate Committee on Banks and the Select Majority Task Force on Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises, and is running unopposed for re-election.

background.text: Raised in Hammel Houses, a public housing development in the Rockaways, in Southeast Queens.
Graduated from Far Rockaway High School and earned a bachelor's degree in history, with a specialization in African-American studies, from Brooklyn College in 1984.
Served in the U.S. Marine Corps.
Worked in the office of U.S. Representative Floyd H. Flake before entering elected office.
Served as President of Queens School Board District 27, becoming the first African-American to lead the board.
Elected to the New York City Council representing District 31 in 2001 and served until 2012, becoming the first African-American chair of the Council's Economic Development Committee.

priorities.text: Expanding access to capital and contracting opportunities for minority- and women-owned businesses, saying "MWBEs deserve meaningful opportunities to grow, compete, and build generational wealth."
priorities.quote: MWBEs deserve meaningful opportunities to grow, compete, and build generational wealth.

priorities.text: Protecting vulnerable New Yorkers, including through elder-abuse prevention training requirements and a task force on school transportation safety.
Expanding financial inclusion, including a bill to allow state deposits in Minority Depository Institutions and a bill barring banks from charging ATM fees on Electronic Benefit Transfer cards.

record.text: Chairs the Senate Committee on Banks and the Select Majority Task Force on Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises; also serves on the Commerce, Economic Development and Small Business, Insurance, Labor, Racing, Gaming and Wagering, and Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs committees.
Sponsored S876, requiring modification of restrictive covenants prior to real property sales; signed into law.
Sponsored S8789, prohibiting employers, labor organizations and employment agencies from using consumer credit history in hiring decisions; signed into law.
Introduced S3071A in March 2026 to establish a statewide Task Force on Safety in School Transportation.
Voted yes on S9500-A (GREAT Act), establishing the New York State grid reliability and energy affordability transition program, which passed the Senate 39–21.
Voted yes on S8455-B, restricting the sale of flare guns and creating related criminal offenses, which passed the Senate 35–25.

Sponsored a package of bills that passed both houses in 2026, including reciprocal recognition of NYC and state MWBE certifications, stronger MWBE utilization-plan accountability on public contracts, and reduced allowable levels of coal tar chemicals in pavement sealants.
